answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Short easy runs can start this week, as the plan shows. Only start the Wednesday run if stairs and walking feel normal; if they don't, walk 20 minutes instead. Expect to be back to a normal weekly routine in about three weeks, with hard running only after that.

A 10K on Nov 26 is possible, but treat it as a tune-up rather than a goal, and do not commit yet. That race is about five and a half weeks after the marathon. A 10K at race effort needs two short quality sessions in the weeks before, so that work would need to start around the week of Nov 2 – 8. Tell me at your next check-in whether you want that race or a longer break from racing, and I will build from there.

new.analysis:
## What the week shows
The week of Oct 12 – 18 ran as planned on distance. Each run landed within about 0.1 mi of its target, and both rest days were taken. The Wednesday session was run as four fast reps totaling about 2 mi at 8:34/mi. That matches the plan's 2 miles at marathon pace in total, so the sharpening work was sound.

## The race
Your first 20 miles were on target, and the miss came in the last six. The table shows where the time went.

| Segment | Pace | Against goal pace of 8:35/mi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Miles 1 – 20 | about 8:32/mi | about 3 seconds per mile faster |
| Miles 20 – 26.2 | about 9:28/mi | about 53 seconds per mile slower |
| Finish | 3:50 | 5 minutes over the 3:45 target |

Going out at goal pace was the right call, so the fade is the thing to learn from. Your quads gave out after mile 20, which points more to leg durability than to aerobic fitness. Your heart rate drifted only 6.5 bpm, and that fits a fitness base that held while the legs did not. Your peak week was about 41 miles with one 20-mile run, so the last six miles were the part of the marathon your training had not yet rehearsed. The overload notice on the race week is the race itself, not a sign the training was too heavy.

## Why ease for two weeks
Soreness from a full marathon usually takes one to two weeks to clear, and hard stairs mean your legs are still in that stage. This week is about 6.5 miles of easy running, roughly a sixth of race week, with no quality work. Keeping easy runs under 135 bpm, below the 138 you averaged before the race, gives tired legs room to recover. You averaged 6.5 hours of sleep in race week, so the plan fills the other days with walking rather than extra load.

safetyCallouts.title: Calves and the toe blister need watching.
safetyCallouts.body: Calf soreness after a marathon is common, but calf pain that sharpens, swells, or worsens each day needs a qualified professional before you run again.

safetyCallouts.title: A blister that looks red, hot, or drains should be checked by a qualified professional rather than managed at home.
